business_question: Which subscribers are about to leave, and for which of them is a retention offer actually worth making?
success_criteria: PR-AUC materially above the 0.265 prevalence floor and above an analyst heuristic.
Probabilities calibrated well enough to multiply by a dollar amount.
A campaign that nets positive value on held-out customers.
No group fails the four-fifths rule at the deployed threshold.

phases.title: 1. Business Understanding
phases.purpose: Translate a business question into a measurable data-mining goal and fix the success criteria before seeing any results.
phases.summary: The deliverable is not a churn score, it is a contact list. That reframing drives every later decision: the probability must be calibrated because it gets multiplied by margin, and the threshold must come from the cost asymmetry rather than from convention.
activities: Framed the output as a ranked contact list with a spend decision.
Elicited the retention economics and wrote them down as assumptions.
Chose PR-AUC as the selection metric given 26.5% prevalence.
Declared gender, senior-citizen and partner status as audit-only.

findings.statement: Cost asymmetry is roughly an order of magnitude
findings.evidence: missing a churner costs 3x a wasted incentive
findings.implication: A 0.5 threshold would be far too conservative.

decisions.rationale: Prevalence is 26.5%; PR-AUC tracks how well the minority class is ranked, which is the whole task.
decisions.rejection_reason: 73.5% is achievable by predicting 'stays' for everyone, which produces an empty contact list.

decisions.decision: Treat retention economics as explicit, editable assumptions.
decisions.rationale: They are estimates; the UI lets a reader change them and watch the recommended threshold move.
decisions.rejection_reason: Silently assumes a false positive and a false negative cost the same, which is never true here.

criteria: Business objective is a decision, not a score

phases.title: 2. Data Understanding
phases.purpose: Acquire the data, describe it honestly, and surface quality problems early enough that they can change the plan.
phases.summary: 7,043 subscribers, 21 fields, 11 missing cells. Quality grade A. Churn is heavily concentrated in month-to-month contracts and short tenure.
activities: Profiled every field and cross-tabulated churn by segment.
Built the empirical retention curve by tenure month.
Checked the 11 blank TotalCharges cells against tenure.

findings.statement: All blank TotalCharges belong to tenure-0 customers
findings.implication: Structurally missing, not randomly missing; left as NaN for pipeline imputation.

findings.statement: Contract type is the single strongest segment signal
findings.evidence: month-to-month churn far exceeds two-year churn
findings.implication: Confirms the analyst heuristic is a fair baseline.

findings.statement: Churn risk decays sharply with tenure
findings.implication: Motivated tenure bucketing and the charges-per-tenure ratio feature.

decisions.rationale: Imputing before the split fits a median on test rows.
decisions.rejection_reason: Convenient, but it is a fitted decision disguised as a constant, and it hides the pattern.

phases.title: 3. Data Preparation
phases.purpose: Construct the modelling dataset: selection, cleaning, feature engineering and the train/test protocol that makes evaluation trustworthy.
phases.summary: 21 features: 8 engineered numerics and 13 categoricals. customerID dropped; three sensitive attributes held out for audit. Stratified 80/20 split preserving the 26.5% rate.
activities: Dropped customerID as a pure identifier.
Built charges-per-tenure, service count and tenure buckets.
One-hot encoded categoricals inside the pipeline.
Stratified the split to hold prevalence constant across folds.

findings.statement: customerID is unique for every row
findings.implication: Excluded: a tree given it memorises the training set and generalises to nothing.

findings.evidence: 3 columns routed to the audit only
findings.implication: Measured for disparity without being modelled on.

decisions.decision: Stratify the split on the target.
decisions.rationale: At 26.5% positive on 7k rows, an unlucky shuffle shifts prevalence enough to move PR-AUC materially.
decisions.rejection_reason: Adds avoidable variance to every comparison.

criteria: All fitted transforms inside the Pipeline

phases.title: 4. Modeling
phases.purpose: Select techniques, search their hyperparameters, and record what was tried -- including what failed.
phases.summary: 95 hill-climbing trials over 6 families on cross-validated average precision, then Caruana greedy ensembling over out-of-fold predictions. 'XGBoost' was deployed.
activities: Hill-climbed each family on 5-fold stratified CV.
Generated out-of-fold predictions for greedy ensemble selection.
Fitted isotonic and Platt calibrators on inner folds.
Searched the threshold grid against the cost matrix.

findings.statement: Greedy ensembling added little over the best single model
findings.implication: Families agree closely on this dataset; the single model ships for simplicity.

findings.statement: Calibration barely moved the ranking metrics
findings.evidence: PR-AUC changed marginally while ECE went 0.0177 -> 0.0100
findings.implication: Exactly as theory predicts: calibration is monotone, so it fixes probabilities without reordering them.

decisions.rationale: Chosen on ECE because the probability is multiplied by a dollar amount downstream.
decisions.rejection_reason: Ranks well but is not a probability, so the expected-value calculation would be wrong.

decisions.rationale: Minimises expected cost under the stated economics.
decisions.rejection_reason: Implicitly assumes symmetric costs and would leave most recoverable churners uncontacted.

criteria: Calibrator fitted on inner folds only
Threshold derived from cost, not convention

phases.title: 5. Evaluation
phases.purpose: Assess results against the business criteria from phase 1, not just the loss function, and review the whole process for defects.
phases.summary: Hold-out PR-AUC 0.660 against a 0.539 best baseline and a 0.265 prevalence floor. At the deployed threshold recall is 82.1% at 51.4% precision. The simulated campaign nets $11,597.
activities: Scored the untouched hold-out once.
Simulated campaigns at every targeting depth from 5% to 100%.
Audited disparity across three sensitive attributes.
Compared permutation against impurity importance.

findings.statement: The model beats the analyst heuristic
findings.implication: Justifies the modelling effort over a rule sheet.

findings.evidence: optimum is the top 35% by risk
findings.implication: The ranking, not the classification, is the product.
Reported across all three attributes with the impossibility trade-off stated.

decisions.decision: Report the campaign value curve, not just PR-AUC.
decisions.rationale: A stakeholder decides how many people to contact, not what average precision to accept.
decisions.rejection_reason: Leaves the actual business decision unanswered.

criteria: Beats prevalence floor and analyst heuristic
Fairness measured on all declared attributes

phases.title: 6. Deployment
phases.purpose: Ship the model behind an interface, with monitoring, documented limits, and a plan for the day the data drifts.
phases.summary: Served at /api/projects/churn/predict, returning a calibrated probability, the expected value of an offer and a SHAP breakdown. The threshold travels with the model as configuration.
activities: Pickled the calibrated pipeline.
Exposed an expected-value endpoint the UI drives interactively.
Documented the economic assumptions in the model card.
Set drift monitors on tenure and contract mix.

findings.statement: The threshold is configuration, not a constant
Static snapshot with no time dimension
findings.implication: Cannot detect seasonality or campaign effects; documented as a limitation.

decisions.decision: Return the expected-value calculation, not just the probability.
decisions.rationale: The consumer of this API wants an action.
decisions.rejection_reason: Pushes the cost model into every caller, where it would drift out of sync.

iteration_notes: The first pass used a 0.5 threshold and reported 80% accuracy. The evaluation review rejected it: at that cut the model contacted too few churners to fund the campaign. Introducing the cost matrix sent us back to phase 1 to write the economics down properly.
Calibration was added after noticing that ranking was strong while predicted probabilities systematically understated observed churn.
methodology: CRISP-DM (Cross-Industry Standard Process for Data Mining), Chapman et al. 2000. Phases are iterative; the notes below record where this project looped back rather than proceeding linearly.
